q: What colour is the ceiling inside Notre-Dame Basilica?
funFact: Thousands of gold stars are painted across that blue ceiling.

q: Which giant instrument has thousands of pipes in the basilica?
funFact: The Notre-Dame organ has around seven thousand pipes.

q: Montréal metro trains are unusual because they roll on what?
funFact: Rubber tires make the ride quieter and help on slopes.

q: Which busy station is where three metro lines meet?
funFact: Green, orange and yellow lines all stop at Berri-UQAM.

q: Which colour is the metro line at Guy-Concordia station?
funFact: The green line runs right across the island of Montréal.

q: Who was Jacques Cartier, the man the square is named after?
funFact: He sailed up the St. Lawrence River back in 1535.

q: What are the old streets of Old Montréal paved with?
funFact: Cobblestones are bumpy — that is why carriages rattle.

q: The Montréal Science Centre sits right beside what?
funFact: Real cargo ships once tied up at that very pier.

q: A cannoli is a sweet treat from which country?
funFact: Montréal's Mile End is full of Italian cafés like Olimpico.

q: In what year did Canada become a country?
funFact: Notre-Dame Basilica was already finished long before that.
